sanskrit: kṛtābhiṣeko rāmas tu sītā saumitrir eva ca tasmād godāvarītīrāt tato jagmuḥ svam āśramam
english: Having performed the ablution ritual, Rāma together with Sītā and Saumitri departed from that bank of the Godāvarī and proceeded to their own hermitage.

sanskrit: āśramaṃ tam upāgamya rāghavaḥ sahalakṣmaṇaḥ kṛtvā paurvāhṇikaṃ karma parṇaśālām upāgamat
english: Having reached that hermitage, Rāghava together with Lakṣmaṇa performed the morning religious rites and entered the leaf-hut.

sanskrit: sa rāmaḥ parṇaśālāyām āsīnaḥ saha sītayā virarāja mahābāhuś citrayā candramā iva lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā cakāra vividhāḥ kathāḥ
english: That great-armed Rāma, seated in the leaf-hut with Sītā, shone like the moon adorned with stars; together with his brother Lakṣmaṇa he engaged in various conversations.

sanskrit: tadāsīnasya rāmasya kathāsaṃsaktacetasaḥ taṃ deśaṃ rākṣasī kā cid ājagāma yadṛcchayā
english: While Rāma sat there with his mind absorbed in conversation, a certain rākṣasī came to that place by chance.

sanskrit: sā tu śūrpaṇakhā nāma daśagrīvasya rakṣasaḥ bhaginī rāmam āsādya dadarśa tridaśopamam
english: She was Śūrpaṇakhā by name, sister of the rākṣasa Daśagrīva; approaching Rāma, she beheld him who resembled a god.

sanskrit: siṃhoraskaṃ mahābāhuṃ padmapatranibhekṣaṇam sukumāraṃ mahāsattvaṃ pārthivavyañjanānvitam
english: He had the chest of a lion, great arms, and eyes resembling lotus petals; he was tender of form, of great essence, and bore the marks of a sovereign.

sanskrit: rāmam indīvaraśyāmaṃ kandarpasadṛśaprabham babhūvendropamaṃ dṛṣṭvā rākṣasī kāmamohitā
english: Beholding Rāma, dark as the blue lotus, radiant as the god of love, comparable to Indra himself, the rākṣasī was overpowered by passion.

sanskrit: sumukhaṃ durmukhī rāmaṃ vṛttamadhyaṃ mahodarī viśālākṣaṃ virūpākṣī sukeśaṃ tāmramūrdhajā
english: He was fair-faced while she was ugly-faced; he had a trim waist while she was great-bellied; he had wide eyes while she had misshapen eyes; he had beautiful hair while her locks were copper-red.

sanskrit: priyarūpaṃ virūpā sā susvaraṃ bhairavasvanā taruṇaṃ dāruṇā vṛddhā dakṣiṇaṃ vāmabhāṣiṇī
english: He was lovely in form while she was disfigured; he had a beautiful voice while she had a terrifying voice; he was young while she was old and fearsome; he was gentle while she spoke ill.

sanskrit: nyāyavṛttaṃ sudurvṛttā priyam apriyadarśanā śarīrajasamāviṣṭā rākṣasī rāmam abravīt
english: He was righteous in conduct while she was deeply wicked; he was pleasing while she was unpleasant to behold. Possessed by passion born of the body, the rākṣasī addressed Rāma:

sanskrit: jaṭī tāpasarūpeṇa sabhāryaḥ śaracāpadhṛk āgatas tvam imaṃ deśaṃ kathaṃ rākṣasasevitam
english: "You have come to this region which is frequented by rākṣasas, wearing matted locks in the guise of an ascetic, accompanied by a wife, bearing a bow and arrows — how so?"

sanskrit: evam uktas tu rākṣasyā śūrpaṇakhyā paraṃtapaḥ ṛjubuddhitayā sarvam ākhyātum upacakrame
english: Thus addressed by the rākṣasī Śūrpaṇakhā, the scorcher of foes, with his straightforward nature, began to tell her everything.

sanskrit: āsīd daśaratho nāma rājā tridaśavikramaḥ tasyāham agrajaḥ putro rāmo nāma janaiḥ śrutaḥ
english: "There was a king named Daśaratha, of the valor of the gods; I am his eldest son, known among men by the name Rāma."

sanskrit: bhrātāyaṃ lakṣmaṇo nāma yavīyān mām anuvrataḥ iyaṃ bhāryā ca vaidehī mama sīteti viśrutā
english: "This is my younger brother named Lakṣmaṇa, devoted to following me; and this is my wife, the Vaidehī, celebrated by the name Sītā."

sanskrit: niyogāt tu narendrasya pitur mātuś ca yantritaḥ dharmārthaṃ dharmakāṅkṣī ca vanaṃ vastum ihāgataḥ
english: "By the command of the king my father, and constrained by my mother as well, desiring righteousness and seeking the good of dharma, I have come here to dwell in the forest."

sanskrit: tvāṃ tu veditum icchāmi kathyatāṃ kāsi kasya vā iha vā kiṃnimittaṃ tvam āgatā brūhi tattvataḥ
english: "But I wish to know about you — tell me, who are you, whose are you? And what is the reason for your coming here? Tell me the truth."

sanskrit: sābravīd vacanaṃ śrutvā rākṣasī madanārditā śrūyatāṃ rāma vakṣyāmi tattvārthaṃ vacanaṃ mama
english: The rākṣasī, tormented by passion, having heard his words, said: "Listen, O Rāma — I shall speak to you words that are true in meaning."

sanskrit: ahaṃ śūrpaṇakhā nāma rākṣasī kāmarūpiṇī araṇyaṃ vicarāmīdam ekā sarvabhayaṃkarā
english: "I am a rākṣasī named Śūrpaṇakhā, able to take any form at will; I roam this forest alone, instilling terror in all."

sanskrit: rāvaṇo nāma me bhrātā rākṣaso rākṣaseśvaraḥ pravṛddhanidraś ca sadā kumbhakarṇo mahābalaḥ
english: "I have a brother named Rāvaṇa, a rākṣasa, lord of the rākṣasas; and Kumbhakarṇa, ever deep in slumber, of great strength."

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇas tu dharmātmā na tu rākṣasaceṣṭitaḥ prakhyātavīryau ca raṇe bhrātarau kharadūṣaṇau
english: "Then there is Vibhīṣaṇa, righteous of soul, not given to rākṣasa ways; and my brothers Khara and Dūṣaṇa, both renowned for their valor in battle."

sanskrit: tān ahaṃ samatikrāntā rāma tvāpūrvadarśanāt samupetāsmi bhāvena bhartāraṃ puruṣottamam cirāya bhava bhartā me sītayā kiṃ kariṣyasi
english: "Surpassing all of them, O Rāma, upon seeing you for the first time I have come with my heart set on you as my husband, O best of men. Be my husband at last — what will you do with Sītā?"

sanskrit: vikṛtā ca virūpā ca na seyaṃ sadṛśī tava aham evānurūpā te bhāryārūpeṇa paśya mām
english: "She is deformed and disfigured — she is not a fitting match for you; I alone am a proper match for you. Regard me in the form of a wife."

sanskrit: imāṃ virūpām asatīṃ karālāṃ nirṇatodarīm anena saha te bhrātrā bhakṣayiṣyāmi mānuṣīm
english: "I shall devour this deformed, wicked, hideous, shrunken-bellied human woman together with your brother here."

sanskrit: tataḥ parvataśṛṅgāṇi vanāni vividhāni ca paśyan saha mayā kānta daṇḍakān vicariṣyasi
english: "Then, beholding mountain peaks and various forests, you shall wander through the Daṇḍakas with me, O beloved."

sanskrit: ity evam uktaḥ kākutsthaḥ prahasya madirekṣaṇām idaṃ vacanam ārebhe vaktuṃ vākyaviśāradaḥ
english: Thus addressed, Kākutstha, skilled in speech, laughed at the intoxicated-eyed one and began to speak these words.

sanskrit: tāṃ tu śūrpaṇakhāṃ rāmaḥ kāmapāśāvapāśitām svecchayā ślakṣṇayā vācā smitapūrvam athābravīt
english: Then Rāma, with a smile and smooth words at his pleasure, addressed Śūrpaṇakhā who was ensnared in the noose of passion:

sanskrit: kṛtadāro 'smi bhavati bhāryeyaṃ dayitā mama tvadvidhānāṃ tu nārīṇāṃ suduḥkhā sasapatnatā
english: "I am already married, dear lady; this is my beloved wife. For women of your kind, the condition of co-wifehood is very difficult to bear."

sanskrit: anujas tv eṣa me bhrātā śīlavān priyadarśanaḥ śrīmān akṛtadāraś ca lakṣmaṇo nāma vīryavān
english: "This younger brother of mine, virtuous, handsome, endowed with prosperity, and not yet married, is named Lakṣmaṇa, a man of valor."

sanskrit: apūrvī bhāryayā cārthī taruṇaḥ priyadarśanaḥ anurūpaś ca te bhartā rūpasyāsya bhaviṣyati
english: "Without a wife as yet and seeking one, young and handsome — this one would make a fitting husband for a beauty such as yours."

sanskrit: enaṃ bhaja viśālākṣi bhartāraṃ bhrātaraṃ mama asapatnā varārohe merum arkaprabhā yathā
english: "Seek this brother of mine as your husband, O wide-eyed one, O fine-hipped one — without a rival co-wife, like the sun's radiance on Mount Meru."

sanskrit: iti rāmeṇa sā proktā rākṣasī kāmamohitā visṛjya rāmaṃ sahasā tato lakṣmaṇam abravīt
english: Thus addressed by Rāma, the rākṣasī bewildered by passion suddenly turned away from Rāma and spoke to Lakṣmaṇa:

sanskrit: asya rūpasya te yuktā bhāryāhaṃ varavarṇinī mayā saha sukhaṃ sarvān daṇḍakān vicariṣyasi
english: "I, of excellent complexion, am a fitting wife for your beauty; with me you shall wander through all the Daṇḍakas in happiness."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu saumitrī rākṣasyā vākyakovidaḥ tataḥ śūrpaṇakhīṃ smitvā lakṣmaṇo yuktam abravīt
english: Thus addressed by the rākṣasī, Saumitri, skilled in speech, smiled at Śūrpaṇakhā and replied with fitting words:

sanskrit: kathaṃ dāsasya me dāsī bhāryā bhavitum icchasi so 'ham āryeṇa paravān bhrātrā kamalavarṇinī
english: "How would you wish to become the wife of a servant like me? I am subject to my noble elder brother, O lotus-complexioned one."

sanskrit: samṛddhārthasya siddhārthā muditāmalavarṇinī āryasya tvaṃ viśālākṣi bhāryā bhava yavīyasī
english: "Become the junior wife of that noble one who has accomplished his purpose and is rich in attainment; rejoice in your spotless beauty, O wide-eyed one."

sanskrit: etāṃ virūpām asatīṃ atimattāṃ mahodarīm bhāryāṃ vṛddhāṃ parityajya tvām evaiṣa bhajiṣyati
english: "Abandoning this deformed, wicked, utterly infatuated, great-bellied, old wife, he will surely take you as his own."

sanskrit: ko hi rūpam idaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ saṃtyajya varavarṇini mānuṣeṣu varārohe kuryād bhāvaṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ
english: "For what wise man, O fine-complexioned one, O fine-hipped one, would direct his affection toward a human woman, forsaking this exquisite beauty of yours?"

sanskrit: iti sā lakṣmaṇenoktā karālā nirṇatodarī manyate tad vacaḥ satyaṃ parihāsāvicakṣaṇā
english: Thus addressed by Lakṣmaṇa, that hideous shrunken-bellied one, inexperienced in mockery, took his words to be true.

sanskrit: sā rāmaṃ parṇaśālāyām upaviṣṭaṃ paraṃtapam sītayā saha durdharṣam abravīt kāmamohitā
english: She, bewildered by passion, then addressed Rāma, the scorcher of foes, who sat in the leaf-hut — formidable even alongside Sītā:

sanskrit: imāṃ virūpām asatīṃ karālāṃ nirṇatodarīm vṛddhāṃ bhāryām avaṣṭabhya na māṃ tvaṃ bahu manyase
english: "Clinging to this deformed, wicked, hideous, shrunken-bellied, old wife, you do not regard me highly."

sanskrit: adyemāṃ bhakṣayiṣyāmi paśyatas tava mānuṣīm tvayā saha cariṣyāmi niḥsapatnā yathāsukham
english: "Today I shall devour this human woman before your eyes; then I shall roam with you without a rival, at perfect ease."

sanskrit: ity uktvā mṛgaśāvākṣīm alātasadṛśekṣaṇā abhyadhāvat susaṃkruddhā maholkā rohiṇīm iva
english: Having spoken thus, with eyes blazing like firebrands, she rushed in great fury at the deer-eyed Sītā, like a great meteor rushing at the star Rohiṇī.

sanskrit: tāṃ mṛtyupāśapratimām āpatantīṃ mahābalaḥ nigṛhya rāmaḥ kupitas tato lakṣmaṇam abravīt
english: The mighty Rāma, enraged, seized her as she charged like the noose of Death, and then spoke to Lakṣmaṇa:

sanskrit: krūrair anāryaiḥ saumitre parihāsaḥ kathaṃ cana na kāryaḥ paśya vaidehīṃ kathaṃ cit saumya jīvatīm
english: "With cruel and ignoble beings, O Saumitri, one must never jest. See how the Vaidehī barely escapes with her life, O gentle one."

sanskrit: imāṃ virūpām asatīm atimattāṃ mahodarīm rākṣasīṃ puruṣavyāghra virūpayitum arhasi
english: "This disfigured, wicked, utterly infatuated, great-bellied rākṣasī — you must disfigure her further, O tiger among men."

sanskrit: ity ukto lakṣmaṇas tasyāḥ kruddho rāmasya paśyataḥ uddhṛtya khaḍgaṃ ciccheda karṇanāsaṃ mahābalaḥ
english: Thus commanded, Lakṣmaṇa, filled with fury, in the sight of Rāma drew his sword and the mighty one cut off her ears and nose.

sanskrit: nikṛttakarṇanāsā tu visvaraṃ sā vinadya ca yathāgataṃ pradudrāva ghorā śūrpaṇakhā vanam
english: With her ears and nose cut off, the dreadful Śūrpaṇakhā let out a discordant shriek and fled into the forest in the direction from which she had come.

sanskrit: sā virūpā mahāghorā rākṣasī śoṇitokṣitā nanāda vividhān nādān yathā prāvṛṣi toyadaḥ
english: That disfigured, most dreadful rākṣasī, drenched in blood, let out various cries like a rain-cloud in the monsoon season.

sanskrit: sā vikṣarantī rudhiraṃ bahudhā ghoradarśanā pragṛhya bāhū garjantī praviveśa mahāvanam
english: Streaming blood on all sides, terrible to behold, she flung up her arms, roaring, and plunged into the great forest.

sanskrit: tatas tu sā rākṣasasaṃghasaṃvṛtaṃ kharaṃ janasthānagataṃ virūpitā upetya taṃ bhrātaram ugratejasaṃ papāta bhūmau gaganād yathāśaniḥ
english: Then, disfigured as she was, she approached Khara who was stationed at Janasthāna surrounded by troops of rākṣasas — that brother of fierce energy — and fell to the ground before him like a thunderbolt falling from the sky.

sanskrit: tataḥ sabhāryaṃ bhayamohamūrchitā salakṣmaṇaṃ rāghavam āgataṃ vanam virūpaṇaṃ cātmani śoṇitokṣitā śaśaṃsa sarvaṃ bhaginī kharasya sā
english: Then, faint with fear and confusion, drenched in blood, that sister of Khara recounted everything to him — the arrival of Rāghava in the forest together with his wife and Lakṣmaṇa, and the mutilation done to her own person.

sanskrit: tāṃ tathā patitāṃ dṛṣṭvā virūpāṃ śoṇitokṣitām bhaginīṃ krodhasaṃtaptaḥ kharaḥ papraccha rākṣasaḥ
english: Seeing his sister fallen thus, disfigured and drenched in blood, the rākṣasa Khara, scorched by wrath, questioned her:

sanskrit: balavikramasaṃpannā kāmagā kāmarūpiṇī imām avasthāṃ nītā tvaṃ kenāntakasamā gatā
english: "You who are endowed with strength and valor, who go where you will, who take any form at will — by whom have you been reduced to this condition, brought to a state equal to death?"

sanskrit: devagandharvabhūtānām ṛṣīṇāṃ ca mahātmanām ko 'yam evaṃ mahāvīryas tvāṃ virūpāṃ cakāra ha
english: "Among gods, gandharvas, spirits, and great-souled sages — who is this one of such great valor who has disfigured you in this way?"

sanskrit: na hi paśyāmy ahaṃ loke yaḥ kuryān mama vipriyam antarena sahasrākṣaṃ mahendraṃ pākaśāsanam
english: "For I see no one in the world who would do harm to me, save for the thousand-eyed Mahendra, the chastiser of Pāka himself."

sanskrit: adyāhaṃ mārgaṇaiḥ prāṇān ādāsye jīvitāntakaiḥ salile kṣīram āsaktaṃ niṣpibann iva sārasaḥ
english: "Today I shall drain his life-breaths with arrows that put an end to life, as a crane sucks up milk clinging to water."

sanskrit: nihatasya mayā saṃkhye śarasaṃkṛttamarmaṇaḥ saphenaṃ rudhiraṃ raktaṃ medinī kasya pāsyati
english: "When he has been slain by me in battle, his vital points severed by arrows, whose frothy red blood shall the earth drink?"

sanskrit: kasya patrarathāḥ kāyān māṃsam utkṛtya saṃgatāḥ prahṛṣṭā bhakṣayiṣyanti nihatasya mayā raṇe
english: "Whose flesh will the birds, gathering joyfully, tear from the body and devour, of him who has been slain by me in battle?"

sanskrit: taṃ na devā na gandharvā na piśācā na rākṣasāḥ mayāpakṛṣṭaṃ kṛpaṇaṃ śaktās trātuṃ mahāhave
english: "Neither gods nor gandharvas, neither piśācas nor rākṣasas will be able to rescue him from my grasp in the great battle, wretched as he will be."

sanskrit: upalabhya śanaiḥ saṃjñāṃ taṃ me śaṃsitum arhasi yena tvaṃ durvinītena vane vikramya nirjitā
english: "Recovering your senses gradually, you must tell me about the one by whom you, arrogant in the forest, were overpowered and defeated."

sanskrit: iti bhrātur vacaḥ śrutvā kruddhasya ca viśeṣataḥ tataḥ śūrpaṇakhā vākyaṃ sabāṣpam idam abravīt
english: Having heard her brother's words, especially his rage, Śūrpaṇakhā then spoke these tearful words:

sanskrit: taruṇau rūpasaṃpannau sukūmārau mahābalau puṇḍarīkaviśālākṣau cīrakṛṣṇājināmbarau
english: "They were two young men endowed with beauty, tender of form yet of great strength, with eyes as wide as white lotuses, wearing bark garments and black antelope skins."

sanskrit: gandharvarājapratimau pārthivavyañjanānvitau devau vā mānuṣau vā tau na tarkayitum utsahe
english: "Resembling the king of the gandharvas, bearing the marks of sovereignty — whether they be gods or humans, I cannot determine."

sanskrit: taruṇī rūpasaṃpannā sarvābharaṇabhūṣitā dṛṣṭā tatra mayā nārī tayor madhye sumadhyamā
english: "I saw there a young woman endowed with beauty, adorned with all ornaments, slender-waisted, standing between the two of them."

sanskrit: tābhyām ubhābhyāṃ saṃbhūya pramadām adhikṛtya tām imām avasthāṃ nītāhaṃ yathānāthāsatī tathā
english: "Those two, acting together on account of that woman, have reduced me to this condition, like a wretched masterless creature."

sanskrit: tasyāś cānṛjuvṛttāyās tayoś ca hatayor aham saphenaṃ pātum icchāmi rudhiraṃ raṇamūrdhani
english: "In the forefront of battle I wish to drink the frothy blood of that one of crooked conduct, and of those two as well, slain there."

sanskrit: eṣa me prathamaḥ kāmaḥ kṛtas tāta tvayā bhavet tasyās tayoś ca rudhiraṃ pibeyam aham āhave
english: "This would be my first wish fulfilled by you, dear brother — that I might drink their blood in battle, hers and those two men's alike."

sanskrit: iti tasyāṃ bruvāṇāyāṃ caturdaśa mahābalān vyādideśa kharaḥ kruddho rākṣasān antakopamān
english: While she was still speaking thus, enraged Khara dispatched fourteen rākṣasas of great strength, resembling Death itself:

sanskrit: mānuṣau śastrasaṃpannau cīrakṛṣṇājināmbarau praviṣṭau daṇḍakāraṇyaṃ ghoraṃ pramadayā saha
english: "Two humans, well-armed, wearing bark garments and black antelope skins, have entered the dreadful Daṇḍaka forest together with a woman."

sanskrit: tau hatvā tāṃ ca durvṛttām upāvartitum arhatha iyaṃ ca rudhiraṃ teṣāṃ bhaginī mama pāsyati
english: "Having slain those two and that wicked woman, you must return; and my sister here shall drink their blood."

sanskrit: manoratho 'yam iṣṭo 'syā bhaginyā mama rākṣasāḥ śīghraṃ saṃpadyatāṃ gatvā tau pramathya svatejasā
english: "This desired wish of my sister — let it be accomplished swiftly, O rākṣasas; go and crush those two by your own might."

sanskrit: iti pratisamādiṣṭā rākṣasās te caturdaśa tatra jagmus tayā sārdhaṃ ghanā vāteritā yathā
english: Thus commanded, those fourteen rākṣasas set out thither together with her, like storm-clouds driven by the wind.
